description: A stereo sampler: a note loud enough to cross a threshold is captured, repeats of it are spawned on a tempo grid, and those repeats run through four effects

params.text: Crossfades between the signal coming in and the repeats, dry at the bottom of its travel and nothing but repeats at the top
Sets how far apart the repeats fall, 100ms to 2 seconds
Inactive at the centre; clockwise each repeat rolls its own dice for a shift up, first an octave and then a fifth above that, and anticlockwise the same shifts go downward
Sets how long the stream of repeats lasts; past about nine tenths of its travel it freezes instead, holding the captured audio and stopping any new capture
Inactive at the centre; anticlockwise the tempo grid lurches into sudden accelerations, clockwise the two previous captures come back as extra layers on every second and every third tick
Inactive at the centre; anticlockwise a wobbling, saturating narrow band, clockwise sample-rate reduction that gets harsher
Inactive at the centre; anticlockwise a deep dark reverb, clockwise an allpass diffusion that melts the attacks together
Inactive at the centre; anticlockwise a low-pass, clockwise a high-pass
Sets how much the loudness of what was played carries into the repeats: at the bottom of its travel every repeat comes out the same, at the top a soft phrase nearly disappears
Sets the level a note has to cross to be captured, 25mV to 5V, starting at playing level so that a bed or a tail does not fire it
Sets the attack of each repeat's envelope, 1ms to 800ms
Sets the release of each repeat's envelope, 5ms to 1500ms
Sets how deep and how fast the lofi knob's wobble runs
Sets the tail length of the reverb or the smear
Sets how wide the repeats are spread, each one landing at its own random position between the two sides
Sends the dry signal through the four effects as well; at the bottom of its travel only the repeats are treated
Holds the captured audio indefinitely and stops any new capture, which is what the top of the sustain knob does too; it latches, so one press holds it
While it is held down, the pitch, lofi and reverb knobs jump to one new random position each, anywhere in their range, and snap back on release
Chooses how a repeat plays: standard, reversed, or the swelling tail of it alone

inputs.text: The left side of the signal to capture
The right side of the signal; with nothing patched here the left jack feeds both sides
Added to the pitch knob; five volts covers half its travel
Added to the sustain knob; ten volts covers its whole travel
Added to the glitch knob; five volts covers half its travel
Added to the filter knob; five volts covers half its travel
A clock the repeat grid follows instead of the tempo knob, measured between rising edges; it is released about ten seconds after the clock stops
While it is high the captured audio is held, as the freeze button does
While it is high the pitch, lofi and reverb knobs are thrown to random positions, as the tilt button does
Added to the tempo knob; ten volts covers its whole travel
A rising edge forces a capture whatever the level is, the capture runs while the gate is high, and the falling edge commits it

outputs.text: The left side of the result; with nothing patched into the right jack this one carries both sides summed
The right side of the result

notes: set the threshold before anything else. The lamp by the capture jack lights while a capture runs: adjust until it lights on your notes and goes dark between them.
a capture starts when the level crosses the threshold and runs until it falls back to about seven tenths of it, or two seconds, whichever comes first.
the captured sound becomes the newest of three slots. The slots and anything frozen never expire, but the buffer is not saved with the patch and is emptied by a change of sample rate.
everything dynamic in this module keys off that threshold, so it is worth treating as part of the gain staging rather than as a knob to set later.
menu: Clock multiplier — scales an external clock by 1/4, 1/2, x1, x2 or x4; it does nothing to the tempo knob
Cap grain to tempo interval — on by default, so a repeat is never longer than one tempo period; off, each repeat replays the whole captured note and the repeats overlap into a wash
Resync grid to capture — Note end, the default, puts the first repeat one tempo interval after the note ends; Note start locks the grid to the attack; Off lets the grid free-run
Clear buffer — empties the three sample slots and whatever is frozen
